candidate_identity: architecture refactor identified by installed-wheel hash and per-game source manifests
method: Identical locked Python 3.14.9 production dependencies; installed wheels, isolated workers outside checkout.
One worker; seeds 0,1,2; all four games; single province and named joint pair; 20 seconds per solver case.
Each worker has a 90-second wall and 4096 MiB RSS guard; wall includes import, preparation, search and validation.
Baseline series ran before candidate series. Candidate timing series ran without overlapping tests, hooks or builds.
A separate 24-case candidate validation/warmup series is retained, but excluded from timing comparisons because hooks overlapped its start.
Solver work is serial. Native worker RSS sampled at 50ms and final Linux high-water RSS retained.
All cases use ordinary requests and independent economic validation. Source hashes intentionally change; exact model identities do not.
Attila sparse identities independently recompiled from each wheel for both workload requests; other model identities read from every native report.
Three timing samples per case are descriptive; seeds vary, revision order was not randomized, and host variability is not controlled.
No full-world speedup claim; the Rome II pair remains FEASIBLE at the allowance, not proved optimal.
